entities.summary:
The Auschwitz-Birkenau State Museum in Oświęcim, Poland, established 1947 in the preserved buildings of the Nazi German concentration and extermination camp complex where approximately 1.1 million people (90% Jewish) were murdered between 1940-1945, is the largest site of mass murder in human history and the world's most important Holocaust memorial — visited by 2.3 million people annually, designated UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1979, and the physical location where 'Auschwitz' became synonymous with the Holocaust itself. The name 'Auschwitz' has become the defining noun of absolute evil in the 20th century.

Auschwitz I (the main camp, opened 1940) was originally built as a Polish political prisoner camp; Auschwitz II-Birkenau (1942) was the largest extermination center, with four gas chamber-crematoria complexes capable of killing 6,000 people per day. 'Selection' on the Birkenau railway ramp (where arriving deportees were separated into those to be killed immediately and those for forced labor) was performed by SS doctors including Josef Mengele. The Zyklon B gas chambers, the massive prisoner barracks, the Appellplatz, the Wall of Death, and the crematoria remains are preserved.

The museum's exhibits include 3,800 kg of human hair (shorn from victims), 110,000 shoes, 12,000 pots and pans, and hundreds of thousands of personal items — the systematic collection of valuables, hair, teeth, and clothing was part of the Nazi industrial murder process. The liberation by Soviet troops (January 27, 1945) is commemorated annually as International Holocaust Remembrance Day. Pope John Paul II, the Dalai Lama, and every major world leader have visited; Israeli school groups make pilgrimage as part of the March of the Living.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Auschwitz-Birkenau is the defining site of 20th-century human evil — where the murder of 1.1 million people was industrialized, and where the Nazi regime's genocidal project is most viscerally preserved: 3,800 kg of human hair and 110,000 shoes that no statistical summary can replace.
